set.body:
Source: 2026-08-03 quality review, verified against current source.

Problem:
ReportedState (core/Observation.scala:85-89) carries state, flags AND truncated. `truncated` records that a CLI surface cut the state expression off with a trailing `+` rather than naming a flag, so it means precisely: the flag list you are holding may be incomplete. SlurmParsers.report sets it at :539.

JobObservation has fields for state and flags but none for truncated, so at SlurmParsers.scala:147-157 the bit is dropped on the floor before anything is serialized. A consumer reading observation.flags cannot tell a complete flag set from a truncated one, and will read the short list as authoritative.

No codec is at fault: the value never reaches one. This is why the 2026-08-03 codec field audit did not surface it, and why owning the codecs by hand would not fix it either.

Why this is not a Phase A edit:
The honest fix adds a field to the public JobObservation, which is shape churn and belongs in the shape window. It would be additive with a default, exactly like reportedCluster (P8.A7), so it is cheap once that window is open.

Rejected alternative: smuggling it through rawFields. That trades a typed incompleteness marker for a stringly-typed one and hides the problem from the type system.

Acceptance:
- A squeue row whose state expression ends in `+` produces an observation a consumer can recognise as having an incomplete flag list.
- A row with a complete expression is distinguishable from it, pinned by a fixture.
- The bit survives the agent wire, with a decoder default that means "not known to be truncated" for peers that predate the field.
set.title: P8.A12: Preserve the truncated-state-expression bit through to the observation
